title: Authorized connections between organizations
description:
Organizations inside one deployment will need to work together, so they need a way to reach each other. This is the feature that punches a hole in the only hard boundary the design has, so it is specified now and built after the authority epic.

`{tenant_id}#channel#{id}` is a physical partition. A connection is a deliberate, narrow exception built from the clip primitive that already exists.

**Four rules, from docs/ORGANIZATIONS.md:**

- Grants name a resource, never an organization. Support may read this channel is a connection; support may reach Legal is a merge.
- A connection is clipped twice: by the granting member's ceiling, and by what the granting organization's owner permits to leave it at all.
- Received authority is borrowed, not owned, which is what makes connections non-transitive. B cannot re-share A's grant with C because B never held it. Without that distinction the boundary leaks one hop at a time.
- Never at the workplace level. A connection reaches a channel or a named resource, never the computer. A shared workplace across organizations collapses the boundary rather than opening a door in it.

**Blocked by the authority epic ba3ea4.** A connection is a clip, and the clip has to exist first.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Starting: blocker (the clip has to exist first) is satisfied — eef4aa ceiling+clip landed. Dispatching Composer 2.5 to write the Gherkin scenarios (a connection between orgs is a clip; routing escalates to the nearest member whose ceiling covers it; stays blocked if no member covers it) so they exist and fail for the right reason. Pure spec, no implementation.
